nodes.description: Wild-type P82/P84 sit immediately adjacent to Z-lines and at costameres. FXR1P is proposed to hold specific structural mRNAs in a translationally repressed state there, as shown for desmoplakin and talin2 in heart, where Fxr1 loss raised both proteins and disrupted costamere architecture. The authors of the founding study propose that deregulated translation of Z-line mRNAs underlies the minicores; the specific skeletal-muscle target mRNAs have not been identified.

nodes.description: Cardiac and skeletal muscle express FXR1P isoforms P82 and P84 that contain exon 15, while other tissues express shorter isoforms that skip it. The CMYO9B variants are frameshifts at the 5' end of exon 15, so the muscle isoforms lose most of their exon-15 sequence while the ubiquitous isoforms are untouched, which fits the restriction of disease to muscle. In a mouse 5' exon-15 frameshift (dupA) the mutant transcript was reduced to about 31% of control and little P82/P84 protein remained. The biopsy of the founding family lacked the mutant-protein granules seen with the 3' allele that causes CMYO9A, which the authors attribute to low P82/P84 expression. Protein levels have not been measured in CMYO9B patient muscle.
